about: Which clips the synthetic voice must not say (tools/make-tts.py reads this; the measurements are in sound/VOICE.md, «What must stay without audio»). The rows named here are not synthesised and are left out of the manifest the tool writes next to its clips (sound/A1/voz/manifest.json), so tools/make-sound.mjs registers no clip for them and the screens keep their written stand-in there. 'contrasts': the two words of a sound pair (keys …s<n>a and …s<n>b of «Sonido y letra», p<n>.0 and p<n>.1 of Hablar) when the only thing that sets them apart is this: 'nasal' (a tilde on a vowel), 'puso', 'y-i', 'y-u', 'stress'. 'keys': clip keys or patterns (a1u01d2.s*). 'texts': a text that is never said, in any place. 'keep': keys, patterns or texts that --verify must not leave out by itself, once a person has heard the clip and found it right. A line of a dialogue or of a listening item (…l<n>) named here takes its whole clip with it: the clip is put together from its lines, and one that is missing leaves it out, its slow version too. Besides these rules, --verify leaves out by itself every clip of one or two words that a learner hears on its own and that both recognisers hear with wrong letters, and every slow take that is heard worse than the normal take of the same line (the slow version of its listening item is then not put together): the list of a run is in its takes.json and tts-report.json, and the clips are in its folder left-out/. What is named here failed in two runs with different takes, or by a measure no take can pass. A word that is silent as half of a pair is still said where it is a word of a scene, unless its text is named. Every recording that stays silent waits as a clip in the takes folder's left-out/ (sound/A1/voz/left-out), for a listener. Once a native speaker has heard one there and found it right: take its entry out of 'keys', 'texts' or 'contrasts' if one names it, and name it under 'keep' if it is a clip of one or two words that plays on its own (both recognisers heard those wrong, so the tool keeps them out by ear and says so, until 'keep' names them); a slow take or a word that --verify left out needs 'keep' alone. Then run the line of sound/VOICE.md, «How to make the clips again»: the clip comes back from left-out/ as it is, the very file that was heard, without the voice or the recognisers being run. A rule comes before the ear, and 'keep' overrides the ear only: a row that 'keys', 'texts' or 'contrasts' still name stays silent. Since 17 November two more things are read here, by tools/hear-sound.py, which hears every clip as the app plays it (decoded from its MP3, three hearings; sound/VOICE.md, «The ear's test on what ships»). 'words': the flawed word of a clip that 'keys' names (aike of «Ikatúpa aike?», irũ of «che irũ», mbo'ehaópe, Argentina-gua, Héẽ); with 'texts' they are the words the voice must not say alone, and so must not say inside a sentence either: a line that holds one, and in whose MP3 both recognisers write that very word with wrong letters in two hearings of three, is said again with other seeds and, if no take passes, silenced by key (a line of a listening item is not silenced by the tool: a person rules on it, since its whole item goes with it). 'forms': for a Teach example whose point is one letter or one small word (nde / ne, -pe / -me, -kuéra / -nguéra, nd- / n-, ja- / ña-, a prefix of person, ko / pe / amo), 'says' is the example and 'not' the same line as its lesson says it must NOT be said; a clip whose MP3 both recognisers hear nearer to a 'not' line than to the example, in two hearings of three, is said again and, if no take passes, silenced by key. 'acute', in the same entries: the words of the example whose stress its lesson marks with an acute (Jajotopáta, Ikatúpa, mbo'ehaópe, Mávapa, the plurals in -kuéra); a clip in whose MP3 no recogniser writes that acute, in two hearings of three, is treated the same way (a recogniser leaves an acute out of real speech too, so one that writes it is enough). A take that is said again passes when it passes --verify, its MP3 fails none of these rules, and its line is not heard worse as a whole than that of the take it replaces (a take can mend one word and spoil another). A new lesson with such a point gets its examples listed here. The tool itself adds to 'keys' and 'why' when it silences a clip, and writes this file as plain JSON.

why.nasal: The voice says ã ẽ ĩ õ ũ ỹ differently from a e i o u y, but by pitch: the nasal word's last vowel is 1.4 to 4.4 semitones higher in all nine twins measured, while A1−P0, a standard sign of nasality, falls 0 to 4.5 dB for a written ã, where an a after m or n in the same voice falls 8 to 10 dB. The recognisers hear ĩ (petĩ 17 hearings of 18) and often ũ (pytũ 17 of 22), not ã or õ (pytã 0 of 22, tetã 0 of 18, mokõ 0 of 10). A pair whose point is «el aire sale también por la nariz» would teach the learner to listen for the wrong thing. Today: unit 1 day 2 (four pairs), day 5 (three), day 6 (the first), unit 2 day 4 (the first two), Hablar p0 to p2: 26 rows.
why.a1u01d4.s0?, p4.?: mbo'y / mboy, the first pair of «El puso» and a pair of Hablar: after o the puso of mbo'y has no gap (0 ms of silence, voiced through three quarters of the stretch) and both recognisers write «mbohy» (9 and 8 takes of 11 in the verification, and again in the fix round's run); mboy comes back «mbovy» or «mbo'y». The other puso pairs (ka'i / kái, sevo'i / sevói, po'i / poi) are told apart and stay.
why.a1u02d2.s*, a1u02d6.s1?: «La r, siempre suave» (ru / vúrro, nde réra / karréta, roju / arro) and its review pair: the r that opens ru is a hum of about 50 ms before the vowel, not a tap (heard with r in 1 hearing of 18; «ndu», «du» again in the fix round), and rr is one long tap, never a trill (two closures in 0 takes of 15, where the Spanish voice has two or more in 25 of 25; arro is heard «aro»). The words that play show neither of the lesson's two points.
why.a1u02d3.s3?: tetã / tetãme, the fourth pair of «La tilde con sufijo»: the word that plays, tetã, is heard «teta» by both recognisers in 9 takes of 9 in the verification (by one of the two in the fix round's run): the pair differs by more than a nasal vowel, so the 'nasal' rule does not reach it, but its point is the ã.
why.a1u04d2.s0?, a1u04d6.s1?: óga / ogakuéra, the first pair of «El acento se mueve» and its review pair: the accent of óga, the word that plays, shows in nothing measured and is never written by a recogniser (0 of 16 hearings in the verification, «oga» from both again in the fix round; the large one wrote «ora» in 6 takes of 8).
why.a1u01d6.w.hee: Héẽ as a scene word: the two vowels come out as one short one, «he» and «hé», in both runs (and in 9 of the 14 rows that hold the word). In the lines of dialogues it stays.
why.a1u01d6.w.ikatupa: «Ikatúpa aike?» as a scene word: the k before e is heard t, «aite», by both recognisers in both runs.
why.a1u03d3.w.cheiru: «che irũ» as a scene word: heard «chairũ» by both recognisers in both runs.
why.a1u03d5.p2.x3: «Aike mbo'ehaópe.», a Teach example of two words: heard «mbo'eha upe» and «mbo'ehaúpe» in both runs.
why.a1u01d3.r1.l5*: «Ha'e Argentina-gua.», the line that carries the answer of the listening item of unit 1 day 3 (¿Qué dato de la alumna nueva es correcto? Es de Argentina): both recognisers hear the answer's own word with wrong letters, the r before the h lost («a hentinagua», «ahentinagua»), in the take that was kept and in each of nine further takes (2026-11-10). With the line the whole item goes silent (a1u01d3.r1 and its slow version): Listening then shows the transcript, to be read and answered.
why.a1u02d5.r1.l7*: «Héẽ, ndahái.», the third reply of the «respuesta rápida» of unit 2 day 5 (¿Qué responde Vicente? Nahániri, ndahái. Oky.): Héẽ comes out as one short vowel in 9 takes of 10 for each recogniser («he ndahái», «héndahái»), and without its «sí» the wrong reply is heard as «ndahái», «no voy», which answers the question as well as the right one. With the line the whole item goes silent (a1u02d5.r1 and its slow version).
why.pl.3.l1: «Ag̃uahẽma che rógape. Ka'aru aháta mbo'ehaópe.», the line that carries the answer of the placement check's second listening item (¿Dónde está él ahora? En su casa): both recognisers hear it with wrong letters, and neither hears the ka'aru that puts the school in the afternoon («a aru», «ha aru»; with its k in 1 hearing of 20 over ten takes). The placement measures the learner, so the item goes silent (pl.3) and is read from its transcript, as before. pl.1 and pl.5 stay, and the level exam's a1x.4 and a1x.5: sound/VOICE.md says why.
why.texts: Words that are a clip of their own (a scene word, a word written from dictation in Escribir, a word of a pair) and that both recognisers hear with wrong letters in the best of three takes, in two runs with different takes: okẽ («otẽ», «opẽ», «mopẽ»: right in 0 hearings of 22), ñúme («ndume», «nume»: 6 of 6), angirũ («angiro»: 0 of 10 with its ũ), roju («loi'u», «roiu»), roho («joho»: the r that opens it, 0 of 16), chero'y («cherohy»: the puso after o as h), chemandu'a («che manduha»: the puso after u as h), ñemuhára («ñemohára»). kesu, kamby and peju were on this list after the verification; said run in (tools/make-tts.py, «How a clip is said»), they are heard right by the independent recogniser in 5, 4 and 5 takes of 5 and are said again.
why.words: The flawed word of a clip that 'keys' names, wherever it stands: aike («aite» in «Ikatúpa aike?»: the k before e), irũ («chairũ», and «iiru», «iro» alone), mbo'ehaópe («mbo'ehaúpe», «mboeha ope»), Argentina-gua («ahentinagua»: the r before the h is lost, in the kept take and in nine more), Héẽ (one short vowel, «he», «hẽ»: a hearing with two vowels, with or without a break between them, counts as right).
why.a1u01d3.p2.x1: «Che réra Moisés. Che Argentina-gua.»: in the app's MP3, word «argentina-gua» (a1u01d3.p2.x1: ivan: «cherra moisẽche a hentiragua» / «cherra moisẽche a hentiragua» / «cherra moisẽche 'a hentiragua» | mms: «che réra moisés che ahentinagua» / «che réra moisés che ahentinagua» / «che réra moisés che ahentinagua»). Said again with 12 seeds (tools/hear-sound.py, 2026-11-17), and no take passed: 0 to 11: a1u01d3.p2.x1: word «argentina-gua». The take waits in left-out/.
why.a1u03d1.p1.x3.l1: «Héẽ, chekane'õ ha chero'y.»: in the app's MP3, word «héẽ» (a1u03d1.p1.x3#2: ivan: «héicheka ne'o ha che ru'y» / «héicheka nde'o ha che ru'y» / «héicheka nde'o ha che ro'y» | mms: «he che kane'õ ha che ro'y» / «he che kane'õ ha che ro'y» / «he che kane'õ ha che ro'y»). Said again with 12 seeds (tools/hear-sound.py, 2026-11-17), and no take passed: 0: a1u03d1.p1.x3#2: word «héẽ»; 1: a1u03d1.p1.x3#2: word «chero'y», word «héẽ»; 2: a1u03d1.p1.x3#2: word «héẽ»; 3: a1u03d1.p1.x3#2: word «chero'y», word «héẽ»; 4 to 7: a1u03d1.p1.x3#2: word «héẽ»; 8: a1u03d1.p1.x3#2: word «chero'y», word «héẽ»; 9 to 11: a1u03d1.p1.x3#2: word «héẽ». The take waits in left-out/.
why.a1u03d3.p1.x3: «Che ru chokokue ha che sy ñemuhára.»: in the app's MP3, word «ñemuhára» (a1u03d3.p1.x3: ivan: «cheru chokokue a chesy ñemohára» / «cheru chokokue a chesy ñemohára» / «cheru chokokue a chesy ñemohára» | mms: «che ru chokokue ha che sy ñemohára» / «che ru chokokue ha che sy ñemohára» / «che ru chokokue ha che sy ñemohára»). Said again with 12 seeds (tools/hear-sound.py, 2026-11-17), and no take passed: 0 to 10: a1u03d3.p1.x3: word «ñemuhára»; 11: heard worse as a whole than the take it replaces: 14 letters off, against 9. The take waits in left-out/.
why.by: the verification of 2026-11-10 and the fix round that followed it (sound/VOICE.md); the 'nasal' rule is the first round's; the three lines of listening items (a1u01d3.r1.l5, a1u02d5.r1.l7, pl.3.l1) were named when the whole course was said, the same day. 'words', 'forms' and what tools/hear-sound.py adds: the fixes after the review of 16 November (17 November).
